## 1. What Atlas Is

Atlas is a **multi-tenant SaaS education platform**. Organizations ("Tenants") sign up; each Tenant can operate one or more Academies; each Academy runs Course Management + Student Learning + Instructor Operations + Community features (Announcements/Blog/Forum); each Academy can configure and publish its own public marketing website (Theme Engine + Page Composer + CMS + SEO + a real public runtime resolved by hostname); and Atlas itself (the "Platform") layers subscriptions/billing/provisioning and — as of Prompt 13 — a genuine Platform Owner Control Plane on top.

**Target users**: Platform Owners (Atlas staff operating the whole system across every tenant), Tenant/Organization Owners (customers who purchase Atlas and run one or more Academies), Academy Owners/Staff/Instructors (day-to-day operators of one Academy), Students (learners enrolled in Academy courses), and anonymous public visitors (who see an Academy's published marketing website).

**This repository is frontend only.** Every prompt from Prompt 1 onward has treated the backend as abstract/undocumented-but-contracted: real services, real hooks, real types, real Zod validation, real loading/error/empty states — calling a real (currently non-existent) backend through one real API client (`src/services/api/api-client.ts`). As of Prompt 13, **no domain in this repository fakes success, fakes latency, or fakes data** — this was not always true; §19 documents exactly what was fake before Prompt 13 and how each instance was fixed.

### Major product areas
- **Academy Management**: creation, profile, branding, members, settings, onboarding.
- **Course Management**: CRUD, categories, pricing/visibility, Course Builder (sections/lessons), publish workflow.
- **Student Learning**: discovery, enrollment, curriculum, lessons, progress, quizzes, assignments.
- **Instructor Operations**: dashboard, roster, grading, assessment management.
- **Community**: Announcements, Knowledge Blog, Course Forum.
- **Tenant SaaS Foundation**: subscription/usage/entitlements, Plan/Add-on catalog, Trial Policy.
- **Billing/Payments**: Checkout, Payment (manual transfer, gateway-ready), Platform Payment Review.
- **Provisioning**: Tenant → Academy → Theme → Branding → Subdomain → Domain → Ready state machine.
- **Website/CMS**: Theme Engine (5 themes), Page Composer (11 section types), FAQ/Testimonial content library, SEO resolution hierarchy, structured data.
- **Public Website Runtime**: hostname → Academy → published-config rendering, real navigation, real SEO.
- **Domain/DNS/SSL/CDN readiness**: honest "not configured" status types, no real infrastructure.
- **Platform Owner Control Plane** (built in Prompt 13): Organization/Academy/User admin consoles, Roles & Permissions inspection, real Platform Dashboard/Analytics, Audit Log, Support Operations, Plan/Add-on catalog view, Notifications, Search, Settings, Media Library.

### Technical architecture at a glance
- **Frontend stack**: React 18 + TypeScript, Vite (`@vitejs/plugin-react-swc`), React Router v6, Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui primitives, TanStack Query, React Hook Form + Zod, `react-i18next` (EN/AR, LTR/RTL), `lucide-react` icons, `recharts` (first real consumer wired in Prompt 13's Analytics), axios (wrapped in `apiClient`, never called directly).
- **State/data-fetching**: TanStack Query exclusively. Every read is `useApiQuery`, every write is `useApiMutation` (`src/shared/hooks/`), both thin wrappers standardizing loading/error/toast/cache-invalidation behavior.
- **Layered pattern, mandatory for every domain**: `Component → Hook → Service (extends BaseService) → apiClient → backend (abstract)`.
- **Authentication architecture**: `src/services/identity/` (`AuthenticationService`, `SessionService`, `CurrentUserService`, `TokenService`, `AuthorizationService`), surfaced to the app via `AtlasIdentityProvider`/`useAuth()` (`src/app/providers/identity/`).
- **Authorization architecture**: flat `readonly string[]` permission/role arrays on `CurrentUser`/`OrganizationContext`, checked via `AuthorizationService.hasPermission`/`hasRole` and the `usePermissions()` hook; route-level enforcement via a fail-closed `RouteGuard`.
- **Localization architecture**: `react-i18next`, one JSON file per namespace per language under `src/localization/resources/{en,ar}/`, registered in `src/localization/resources/index.ts` and `TRANSLATION_NAMESPACES` (`src/types/localization.types.ts`). 34 namespaces as of Prompt 13 (was ~26 before), 100% EN/AR key parity verified programmatically.
- **Routing architecture**: `src/app/routes/route-paths.ts` (98 `DASHBOARD_ROUTES` entries as of Prompt 13) + `src/app/routes/AppRouter.tsx` (one lazy-loaded `<Routes>` tree, **plus** a top-level hostname branch since Prompt 11 that mounts `PublicWebsiteRouter` instead of the dashboard tree entirely).
- **Design system**: shadcn/ui primitives in `src/components/ui/`, shared composed components in `src/shared/components/` (layout/feedback/data-display/table/controls/navigation/branding/loading).
- **API/client architecture**: one `apiClient` (`src/services/api/api-client.ts`), one `BaseService` abstract class every domain service extends, one query-key factory registry (`src/services/query/query-keys.ts`).
- **Backend-readiness strategy**: every real domain's service methods are real, typed, callable HTTP calls through `apiClient` against a backend that does not yet exist. Nothing is a mock function standing in for a network call. A backend engineer can implement directly against the method signatures documented in §9.
- **Current development status**: Frontend feature-complete through Prompt 13's stated scope. Zero known frontend gaps from the Prompt 12 audit remain unaddressed (each is either FIXED or explicitly documented as DEFERRED BY SPECIFICATION / SPECIFICATION-UNDEFINED — see §16). No backend exists. No commit in this repository implements backend code.

# Development History

The project was built as a sequence of numbered "Prompts," each a complete, explicit specification message from the project owner, implemented in full before the next began. In this codebase, one Prompt is functionally one development phase — there is no separate "Phase N" numbering distinct from the Prompt numbering. This section presents that history chronologically; §3 ("Prompt History") gives the same information indexed by prompt number for quick lookup, with cross-references.

## Phase 1 / Prompt 1 — Foundation
**NOT VERIFIED IN DETAIL** — predates all visible conversation history and the prior handoff's own visibility. Reconstructed only from `Reports/PROGRESS.md`'s earliest Progress Log entries referring to "Prompt 2 hardening" of pre-existing infrastructure. Established (inferred): the API client layer, `BaseService` pattern, TanStack Query provider setup, identity/auth scaffolding, the routing shell, design tokens, and i18n scaffolding. Exact file list NOT VERIFIED — treat any specific claim with caution and check `src/services/`, `src/app/providers/` directly if precision matters.

## Phase 2 / Prompt 2 — Hardening
**NOT VERIFIED IN DETAIL** — predates visible conversation. Per `Reports/PROGRESS.md`'s Progress Log (2026-08-19): token refresh concurrency deduplication, identity/platform sync, organization-switch cache invalidation, fail-closed authorization, file upload progress/cleanup, `FormData` `Content-Type` handling, feature-flag loading state, removed sensitive logging. This phase is the origin of two rules that hold throughout the entire codebase: fail-closed `RouteGuard`, and organization-switch query invalidation via `PlatformProvider`.

## Phase 3 / Prompt 3 (Parts A, B, C) — Platform Core, Academy Management, Course Management
VERIFIED (Part A verified via direct code inspection during Prompt 12's audit; Parts B/C verified via `Reports/ARCHITECTURE.md`/`Reports/PROGRESS.md`).

**Part A** built 9 features on Prompt 1/2's infrastructure: Auth UI (Sign In/Register/Forgot/Reset Password), User Profile, Role-Based Navigation, Platform Owner Dashboard, Platform Settings, Notifications UI, Billing UI, Analytics UI, Search Experience. `Reports/PROGRESS.md` recorded this as complete with all checks passing at the time. **Critical fact discovered by Prompt 12's audit, and directly relevant to Prompt 13**: five of these nine were UI shells — correct component structure, correct i18n, correct responsive/RTL support, but **no service, no hook, no real data, no working mutation** behind Platform Dashboard, Settings, Notifications, Analytics, or the legacy Billing page. Search was worse: a self-documented mock array with a literal `setTimeout` fake-latency delay. This state persisted, untouched, from Prompt 3A through Prompt 12 — no later prompt's scope included fixing it. **Prompt 13 fixed all of it** (§19).

**Part B** built Academy Dashboard, Creation, Profile, Settings, Branding, Members, Onboarding, Switching, permission-aware navigation. Established `AcademyService`, `academyKeys` (organization-scoped), the Academy-as-sub-resource-of-Organization pattern, and `useFilePicker`+base64 as the only upload mechanism (no upload endpoint exists in any documented contract, then or now). A mid-phase recovery audit found and fixed a dead `requiredCapabilities` nav field, migrated Members to the shared `DataTable`, and fixed a real `RouteGuard` regression (nested guards silently defaulting `requireAuthentication` to `false`) — this exact incident is why "every new route explicitly sets `requireAuthentication`, verified by grep" became standing practice for every subsequent prompt, including Prompt 13.

**Part C** built the full Course domain nested under Academy (`academies/:academyId/courses/...`): CRUD, categories, pricing/visibility, Course Builder (sections + lessons with explicit keyboard-accessible move-up/move-down reordering — no drag-and-drop library exists in the project, and this became the standing reordering pattern for every later domain including Prompt 9's section trees and Prompt 13's Media Library considerations), publish/unpublish workflow, full EN/AR localization. Established `courseKeys` embedding `academyId` directly — the query-key scoping pattern every subsequent Academy-scoped domain copies, including Prompt 13's `mediaKeys`.

## Phase 4 / Prompt 4 — Student Learning & Assessment
VERIFIED. Built the student-facing experience on top of Academy + Course: discovery (a new flat, cross-academy `discoverCourses`/`discoverCourse` pair), enrollment, curriculum navigation, lesson consumption, progress, quizzes, assignments, completion state (no real certificate generation — explicitly deferred). Established the **second distinct service-tree pattern**: Student Learning's flat `courses/:courseId/...` tree, separate from Course Management's academy-scoped tree, because a student reaches a course by id alone. Every query key embeds the current student's id from `useAuth().user.id`, never a parameter. Quiz correct answers are structurally never modeled on `QuizQuestionOption` — a type-level guarantee that must never be weakened.

## Phase 5 / Prompt 5 — Instructor / Teaching Operations + Communication & Knowledge Modules
VERIFIED. Built Instructor Dashboard, My Courses, Course Overview, Student Roster, Student Progress, Assessment Management, Grading, Quiz Results, plus three cross-role modules: Announcements, Knowledge Blog, Course Forum. Established the **third service-tree precedent** (`InstructorService`, flat `instructor/courses/:courseId/...`) — an instructor's teaching scope is resolved server-side from `Course.instructors`, never client-supplied. Grading is gated by a permission separate from viewing. **First naming-collision precedent**: a pre-existing static, unauthenticated marketing blog (`src/lib/blog.ts`, `src/pages/blog/`) already existed; the new dynamic, permission-gated, dashboard-embedded feature was deliberately named "Knowledge Blog" with its own `BlogService`/`BlogPost`, kept explicitly distinct. This precedent recurs through Prompt 11 and is directly relevant to why Prompt 13 kept `@features/billing`'s legacy shell distinct in name from the real payment feature it shares a directory with (until Prompt 13 deleted the legacy shell — §19).

## Phase 6 / Prompt 6 — Atlas SaaS Foundation, Tenancy, Subscriptions, Plans, Entitlements, Usage & Platform Admin
VERIFIED. Turned Atlas into a real multi-tenant SaaS platform. **Organization is the sole Tenant boundary** — no parallel `tenantId`/`TenantContext` was ever introduced, and this remains true through Prompt 13. Built `TenantService` (read-only: `getSubscription`/`getUsage`/`getActiveAddOns`, **zero write methods**, because no payment provider existed yet) and `PlanService` (read-only catalog `getPlans`/`getPlan`/`getAddOns`/`getAddOn`, **plus exactly one write method**, `updateTrialPolicy`). Established `getLimitGapAction`/`getFeatureGapAction` as the one centralized upgrade-vs-add-on decision point. Established the `DEFAULT_TRIAL_POLICY`-as-query-`initialData` idiom (compiled default, immediately marked stale, superseded by the real backend response) — reused for `DEFAULT_PLATFORM_DOMAIN_CONFIGURATION` in Prompt 11.

**Explicit deferral, still true after Prompt 13**: "NO full Plan/Subscription CRUD admin UI." Prompt 13 built a read-only Platform Owner Plan/Add-on catalog VIEW (`PlatformPlanCatalogPage.tsx`) but did not add create/edit/retire mutations, because no such contract exists anywhere in the product specification — this boundary is documented directly in the page's own doc comment (§19/§23).

## Phase 7 / Prompt 7 — Atlas Enterprise Billing & Payment Platform
VERIFIED. Full payment engine on Prompt 6's foundation: `Money`/`SubscriptionBillingCycle`, Checkout domain (frozen commercial snapshot, client-generated idempotency key replayed on retry), Payment domain (one shape for manual and any future gateway payment, discriminated only by capability flags). Provider abstraction (`PaymentProviderAdapter`) with exactly one registered adapter (`ManualTransferProvider`). Three services: `CheckoutService`/`PaymentService` (tenant-scoped) + `PlatformPaymentService` (a third, deliberately flat cross-tenant tree — the Payment Review console). Redirect/return query parameters are never trusted; `PaymentDetailsPage` always re-fetches authoritative status. **Second naming-collision precedent**: discovered `src/features/billing/` already held a Prompt 3A legacy feature; registered Prompt 7's translations under a new `payments` namespace and renamed 4 colliding type names rather than overwriting the legacy feature. That legacy `BillingPage.tsx` remained in the repo, still linked in nav, still fake, all the way until **Prompt 13 deleted it** (§19) — Prompt 7 correctly avoided touching it but never flagged it as needing a fix, which is why it survived to Prompt 12's audit.

## Phase 8 / Prompt 8 — Atlas Provisioning + Academy Lifecycle
VERIFIED. The orchestration domain: Tenant → Academy → Theme → Branding → Subdomain → Domain → Provisioning → Ready. A real, idempotent, resumable state machine — `ProvisioningRequest` carries both a coarse 12-value `ProvisioningStatus` and a real `steps[]` array (7 steps × pending/running/completed/failed/skipped). The `tenant` and `theme` steps are observability-only (Prompt 8 does not create Tenants or implement a Theme Engine; both render `'skipped'` until their owning system exists). `retryProvisioning` deliberately covers both "retry" and "resume." `SubdomainAllocation`/`DomainConnection` model display state only — this exact type vocabulary was reused verbatim by Prompt 11, and by Prompt 13's `PlatformAcademyDetail.provisioningStatus`/`domainStatus` fields.

## Phase 9 / Prompt 9 — Atlas Theme Engine + Website Experience Platform
VERIFIED. The multi-tenant Theme Engine and Page Composer for an Academy's public website. **Third and largest naming-collision precedent**: a pre-existing, unrelated dashboard light/dark `Theme`/`ThemePreference`/`ThemeProvider` system already existed; every new type/file is prefixed `Website*`, never bare `Theme*` — a rule that must never be violated. Built 5 genuinely distinct themes via a bounded design-token system plus structural Hero/Header/Footer variants. `WebsiteConfiguration` (academy-scoped, draft-only) and `WebsitePage` with an 11-type Section Registry. Sections **reference** course/instructor data by id, never copy it. One `WebsiteRenderer` composition root, used identically by the theme gallery, the Page Editor's live preview, and `WebsitePreviewPage`. A descriptor-driven `SectionConfigForm` replaces 11 bespoke editor forms.

## Phase 10 / Prompt 10 — Atlas CMS + SEO Platform
VERIFIED. Structured content management + an independent SEO domain. `LocalizedText` (`{en, ar}`, both required) — Atlas's first user-generated-content localization primitive, scoped only to `WebsiteFaqEntry`/`WebsiteTestimonialEntry`, never retrofitted onto Prompt 9's single-locale strings. Archive is the only removal action — no hard delete anywhere in CMS content. SEO resolution hierarchy established: **Page/Entity Override → Website Global → Atlas System Fallback** — `resolvePageSeo`/`resolveCourseSeo`/`resolveBlogPostSeo` (`src/features/website/utils/seo-resolution.utils.ts`). Only `resolvePageSeo` was wired to a live surface at the time; `resolveCourseSeo`/`resolveBlogPostSeo` were built correctly but orphaned — **Prompt 13 wired `resolveCourseSeo` into the real public Course Details page and documented why `resolveBlogPostSeo` still has no possible consumer** (§19/§23).

## Phase 11 / Prompt 11 — Atlas Public Website Runtime + Full Website CMS + Domain/Cloudflare Readiness
VERIFIED. Four objectives: (A) CMS gap-closure — found `WebsiteCta.url` had been a typed field with zero reachable UI since Prompt 9, fixed additively with a real Link Type selector; (B) the actual public website runtime — `PublicWebsiteRouter` mounted by `AppRouter` instead of the dashboard tree, `resolvePublicWebsiteContext` returning `{mode:'atlas-app'}` whenever no platform domain is configured (true in every environment today), `PublicWebsiteService` as a third, session-less service tree; (C) SEO runtime — `useDocumentSeo` hand-rolls `document.head`, JSON-LD via `textContent` (never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`); (D) Domain/DNS/SSL/CDN readiness — reuses Prompt 8's types verbatim, adds `SslStatus`/`CdnStatus`/`InfrastructureProviderStatus`, every status defaults to "not configured." `@features/website` got its first public barrel.

## Phase 12 / Prompt 12 — Complete Frontend Gap Audit
VERIFIED (executed in the visible conversation, produced **zero code changes** by explicit instruction — "DO NOT IMPLEMENT ANYTHING"). A CTO-style discovery audit of the entire repository against the original brief's Platform Owner responsibilities. Found: 9 domains genuinely Complete; 5 domains presented as delivered in Prompt 3A that were actually static UI shells (Platform Dashboard, Analytics, Settings, Notifications, legacy Billing); 1 domain with self-documented fake data (Search); 8 domains from the Platform Owner brief that were never built in any prompt (Organization Admin Console, Academy Global Console, User Directory, Roles & Permissions, Audit Log, Support Operations, Plan/Add-on Catalog Administration, Media Library). Full findings preserved in §17 of this document (the Prompt 12 → 13 Remediation Matrix).

## Phase 13 / Prompt 13 — Frontend Completion / Full Audit Remediation
VERIFIED — this entire phase is documented in exhaustive first-hand detail in §3 and §4 below, since it is the phase this document's author directly implemented. **This is the most important phase for a future session to understand precisely**, because it is the one that took the repository from "9 complete domains + 5 shells + 1 fake + 8 missing" to "zero known frontend gaps from the Prompt 12 audit." Objective: remediate every P0/P1/P2 finding from Prompt 12, plus a self-directed "small issues" sweep that found and fixed 7 additional fake-`setTimeout` instances the enumerated domains didn't cover (Auth forms, Profile forms, feature-flag loading). Committed as `cd96058` "frontemd fixes" (154 files changed).

VERIFIED, exhaustive first-hand detail. Source: Prompt 12's audit (§17). Explicit rules: frontend only, no fake backend of any kind, must inspect before changing, must preserve the Service→QueryKeys→Hooks→Types/Zod→Pages→Routes/Nav architecture, no second architecture for Platform Owner features, no rewrite of the 9 Complete domains except for real gaps.

**Phase 2 (P0) — Platform Owner Control Plane, part 1:**
- **Organization Admin Console**: `PlatformOrganizationService` (flat `organizations` resource), `usePlatformOrganizations`/`usePlatformOrganization`, `PlatformOrganizationListPage`/`PlatformOrganizationDetailPage`. Instead, `EffectiveAccessSummary`/`EffectiveRoleAssignment`/`EffectivePermissionAssignment` model the caller's OWN effective grants, derived purely from `CurrentUser` (no new fetch). `PlatformRolesPermissionsPage` is an honest inspection view with a boundary `Alert` explaining that no platform-wide catalog/assignment capability exists.

Each fixed with a real mutation against an existing or newly-added `AuthenticationService`/`CurrentUserService` method (§19), or an honest synchronous resolution where no backend contract exists.

- Removed unsupported form fields (`phone`/`bio` in Profile Personal, `marketingEmails` in Profile Preferences) that had no backing contract, rather than leaving them silently unpersisted.
- Rewrote `src/localization/resources/{en,ar}/profile.json` from scratch — the entire namespace was stale relative to the components (a pre-existing, independently-discovered bug, same species as the Analytics/Notifications/Settings key-mismatch bugs already fixed in the named domains).
- Confirmed, via full repository sweep: zero remaining `setTimeout`-as-latency, zero mock/fake data arrays, zero `TODO`/`FIXME`, zero `@ts-ignore`, zero hardcoded platform metrics, zero fake-success-toast-without-mutation patterns, zero `eval`/`new Function`, zero unsafe `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (all 4 repo matches are doc-comments describing its ABSENCE, plus one pre-existing, unrelated, safe shadcn `chart.tsx` internal use), zero orphaned `DASHBOARD_ROUTES` entries, zero duplicate route registrations, 100% EN/AR parity across all 30 (now 34 after Prompt 13) i18n namespaces.

All forbidden-pattern greps return zero hits.

**Final forensic audit**: delivered as chat text at the end of the Prompt 13 conversation turn, per-finding remediation status (FIXED / DEFERRED BY SPECIFICATION / SPECIFICATION-UNDEFINED), reproduced in full in §17 of this document.

# 5. Architecture Map

## Frontend request flow (query)
```
Page
  ↓
Component
  ↓
Hook (useApiQuery, from @/shared/hooks)
  ↓
Query Key (from src/services/query/query-keys.ts — scoped by organizationId/academyId/userId/hostname as appropriate)
  ↓
Service (extends BaseService, src/services/base.service.ts)
  ↓
apiClient (src/services/api/api-client.ts)
  ↓
Backend (abstract — does not exist yet)
```

## Frontend mutation flow
```
Form (React Hook Form)
  ↓
Validation (Zod schema, src/features/<domain>/schemas/)
  ↓
Mutation Hook (useApiMutation, from @/shared/hooks)
  ↓
Service method (POST/PATCH/DELETE via apiClient)
  ↓
apiClient
  ↓
Backend (abstract)
  ↓
onSuccess: query invalidation (invalidateKeys) + optional session refresh (useAuth().refreshSession())
```

## Authentication flow
`AtlasIdentityProvider` (`src/app/providers/identity/IdentityProvider.tsx`) wraps the app, exposing `useAuth()` → `{session, isRestoring, user, organization, isAuthenticated, signIn, signOut, switchOrganization, refreshSession}`. On mount, silently attempts session restoration via `SessionService.restore()`. `signIn`/`signOut` call `SessionService`, which internally uses `AuthenticationService` (real HTTP calls) + `TokenService` (local token storage). `CurrentUserService.getCurrent()` fetches the full `CurrentUser` profile. As of Prompt 13, `AuthenticationService` also exposes `register`/`requestPasswordReset`/`confirmPasswordReset` — real methods, not yet backed by a live backend, consumed by the Auth forms.

## Authorization flow
`AuthorizationService` (`src/services/identity/authorization.service.ts`) operates on flat `readonly string[]` permission/role arrays carried on `CurrentUser.permissions`/`CurrentUser.roles` and `OrganizationContext.permissions`/`.role`. `usePermissions()` (`src/shared/hooks/usePermissions.ts`) exposes `hasPermission`/`hasAllPermissions`/`hasAnyPermission`/`canView`/`canEdit`/`canDelete`/`canManage`, all delegating to `AuthorizationService`. **There is no `Role`/`Permission` entity type anywhere in `src/types`** — Prompt 13's `rbac.types.ts` deliberately does not introduce one (§17/§23), since no catalog contract is specification-defined.

## RouteGuard behavior
`src/app/routes/guards/RouteGuard.tsx` — fail-closed. Every dashboard route wraps its element in `<RouteGuard requireAuthentication ...>`. Accepts `requiredPermissions` (checked via `usePermissions`) and/or `requiredRoles` (checked via `user.roles.includes(...)`, structurally distinct from permission checks — a permission string can never imply the Platform Owner role). Grep-verified count of "N/N RouteGuards set requireAuthentication" has been a standing per-prompt validation step since a Prompt 3B regression; Prompt 13's 13 new routes all set it, gated `requiredRoles: ['platform_owner']`.

## Platform Owner authorization
Every Platform Owner Control Plane route (Organizations/Academies/Users/Roles/Audit Log/Support/Plan Catalog/Dashboard/Analytics/Settings/Domain/Trial Policy/Payment Review/Provisioning) uses `requiredRoles: ['platform_owner']` at the route level — never a permission string. This is structurally distinct from Tenant/Academy-scoped routes, which use `requiredPermissions: [...]`.

## Tenant/Academy scoping
Tenant-scoped data keys on `organizationId` (from `useAuth().organization`). Academy-scoped data keys on `academyId` (from the route param, validated against the user's actual academy memberships server-side). Student-scoped data keys on the current user's own id (`useAuth().user.id`, never a parameter). Public-runtime data keys on hostname/academyId resolved server-side via `resolveHostname` (`useParams` is never used in `@features/public-website`, grep-verified). Platform Owner Control Plane query keys (Prompt 13) are deliberately **unscoped** by organization/academy — they are cross-tenant by design, gated by the `platform_owner` role instead of a scope id.

## Query key scoping (concrete pattern)
```ts
// Tenant-scoped
tenantKeys.subscription(organizationId)
// Academy-scoped
courseKeys.list(academyId, query)
mediaKeys.list(academyId, query)   // Prompt 13
// Student-scoped (never a parameter — read from useAuth() inside the hook)
progressKeys.detail(studentId, courseId)
// User-scoped (Prompt 13, Notifications/Search)
notificationKeys.list(userId, query)
searchKeys.results(userId, query)
// Platform-scoped — deliberately unscoped, cross-tenant by role gate
platformOrganizationKeys.list(query)
auditLogKeys.list(query)
```

## Localization / RTL-LTR
`react-i18next` with `en`/`ar` resource bundles. The active language drives both text direction (`dir="ltr"`/`dir="rtl"`) at the document root and number/date formatting locale (`Intl.NumberFormat`/`Intl.DateTimeFormat` via `LanguageCode`-aware `formatNumber`/`formatCurrency`/`formatPercentage`/`formatBytes` in `src/shared/utils/number.utils.ts`).

## Error handling
`apiClient`/`http-client.ts` normalizes every backend error into one `ApiError` shape with a categorized `ApiErrorKind`. `ErrorState` (`src/shared/components/feedback/ErrorState.tsx`) is the single shared error-presentation component — title/description derived from `kind`, with an optional `onRetry` callback and `requestId` for support traceability. `useApiMutation` auto-shows an error toast by default (`showErrorToast`, opt-out per mutation when the page renders its own contextual error state instead — the pattern used by every Prompt 13 form).

## Loading/empty/error/retry states
Standing convention across every domain: `Skeleton` components for initial loads, `ErrorState` with `onRetry` for query/mutation failures, `EmptyState` (`src/shared/components/feedback/EmptyState.tsx`) for genuinely-empty real results (never for "no service exists yet" — that distinction is exactly what separated the Prompt 3A UI shells from real domains, and is why Prompt 13 was needed).

# 6. Platform Owner Control Plane

*(Note, preserved from the prior handoff: "Platform Owner Control Plane" is this project's own operational grouping for these surfaces — confirmed via targeted grep to NOT be verbatim terminology in `Reports/📘 Atlas AI Constitution.md` or `Reports/Atlas Vision (Volumes 1–6).md`. The underlying responsibilities are drawn from the audit prompts' own stated Platform Owner responsibilities.)*

### 1. Organizations
- **Purpose**: cross-tenant list/search/detail for every Organization on Atlas.
- **Pages**: `PlatformOrganizationListPage.tsx`, `PlatformOrganizationDetailPage.tsx`.
- **Routes**: `/dashboard/platform/organizations`, `/dashboard/platform/organizations/:organizationId`.
- **Service**: `PlatformOrganizationService` (flat `organizations` resource).
- **Hooks**: `usePlatformOrganizations`, `usePlatformOrganization`.
- **Query keys**: `platformOrganizationKeys.list(query)` / `.detail(organizationId)`.
- **Types**: `PlatformOrganizationSummary`, `PlatformOrganizationDetail` (reuses `TenantSubscription`/`TenantUsage` verbatim).
- **Permissions**: route-gated `requiredRoles: ['platform_owner']`.
- **Current state**: FRONTEND COMPLETE, BACKEND PENDING. Read-only.
- **Backend requirements**: `GET /organizations` (paginated, searchable), `GET /organizations/:id` (with subscription/usage/academies/members).
- **Limitations/deferred**: no create/suspend/archive mutation — none is specification-supported.

### 2. Global Academies
- **Purpose**: cross-tenant academy list/detail (distinct from the per-Tenant Academy pages).
- **Pages**: `PlatformAcademyListPage.tsx`, `PlatformAcademyDetailPage.tsx`.
- **Routes**: `/dashboard/platform/academies`, `/dashboard/platform/academies/:academyId`.
- **Service**: `PlatformAcademyService` (flat `platform-academies` resource — deliberately distinct from the tenant-scoped `academies` resource).
- **Hooks**: `usePlatformAcademies`, `usePlatformAcademy`.

# 7. Analytics (dedicated detail)

**Dashboard vs. Analytics distinction**: the Platform Dashboard (`PlatformDashboardPage.tsx`) shows a compact, fixed 7-KPI snapshot plus a 5-item recent-activity feed — a landing overview. Analytics (`AnalyticsPage.tsx`) is a dedicated, tabbed, date-range-filterable exploration surface with time-series charts and a breakdown. They are two different pages, two different services, two different query-key namespaces (`platformMetricsKeys` vs. `analyticsKeys`) — never merged, never sharing a hook.

**Platform Owner analytics**: yes, this is the only analytics surface in the repository. There is no separate Tenant/Academy-facing analytics dashboard as of Prompt 13.

**Metric contracts**: `AnalyticsOverview { totalUsers: AnalyticsMetricTrend, activeUsers: AnalyticsMetricTrend, engagementRatePercent: number, engagementRateChangePercent?: number, revenue: AnalyticsMetricTrend, revenueCurrency: string, generatedAt: string }`, where `AnalyticsMetricTrend = { value: number, changePercent?: number }`.

**Time-series contract**: `AnalyticsTimeSeries { metric: string, points: readonly {date: string, value: number}[] }`.

**Breakdown contract**: `AnalyticsBreakdown { dimension: string, items: readonly {label: string, value: number}[] }`. Only `dimension: 'plan'` is currently wired into the UI (Revenue tab, "Revenue by plan"), but the service method accepts any dimension string.

**Filters/date ranges**: `AnalyticsQuery { dateRange?: {from: string, to: string} }`. The UI offers 3 client-computed presets (7/30/90 days) via `AnalyticsDateRangeSelect`; there is no custom-range picker anywhere in the codebase (none existed as a precedent, and building one was judged out of scope for this remediation pass).

**Chart consumers**: `AnalyticsLineChart` (`recharts`' `LineChart` inside the shared `ChartContainer` primitive from `src/components/ui/chart.tsx`) — the first real consumer of that previously-unused shared component.

**Backend requirements — explicit**:
```
FRONTEND READY
BACKEND PENDING
```
`GET /analytics/overview?from=<date>&to=<date>` → `AnalyticsOverview`
`GET /analytics/time-series/:metric?from=<date>&to=<date>` → `AnalyticsTimeSeries`
`GET /analytics/breakdown/:dimension?from=<date>&to=<date>` → `AnalyticsBreakdown`

None of these endpoints exist. Nothing in Analytics is backend-connected. Every number rendered comes from a real hook wired to a real service method that currently has no backend to call.

# 9. Backend-Ready Contract Inventory

Every service below is a real, typed, callable class extending `BaseService` (or, for identity, a plain class calling `apiClient` directly). None currently has a live backend. "FRONTEND CONTRACT ONLY" means the method signatures are final and a backend engineer can implement directly against them without further frontend changes; "PARTIALLY CONNECTED" means the type/service existed before Prompt 13 and its consumer surface changed; "READY FOR BACKEND" is used interchangeably with "FRONTEND CONTRACT ONLY" in this document — both mean the same thing: **implement the backend to match this shape, do not ask the frontend to change first.**

**Endpoint path note**: every path above is written the way the current frontend calls it (`resourcePath(resource, ...segments)`). None of these are backend-confirmed URLs — they are the frontend's contract proposal. Where a backend team settles on a different path convention, only the `resource`/path-builder strings need to change; no type, hook, or component needs to change.

# 11. Routes and Navigation

`src/app/routes/route-paths.ts` defines 98 `DASHBOARD_ROUTES` entries (plus `PUBLIC_ROUTES`/`AUTH_ROUTES`/`SYSTEM_ROUTES`). `src/app/routes/AppRouter.tsx` is the single lazy-loaded `<Routes>` tree for the authenticated app, **plus** a top-level hostname branch (since Prompt 11) that mounts `PublicWebsiteRouter` instead of this tree entirely when `resolvePublicWebsiteContext` determines the visitor is on a real Academy hostname.

## Route categories
- **Authentication routes** (`AUTH_ROUTES`): sign-in, registration, forgot-password, reset-password. Public, unauthenticated.
- **Tenant/Organization routes**: `/dashboard/tenant/...` — subscription, usage, add-ons, billing, checkout, invoices, payments. Gated `requiredPermissions: ['tenant.*.view']` variants.
- **Academy routes**: `/dashboard/academy/...` — dashboard, profile, settings, branding, members, onboarding, website/*. Gated `requiredPermissions: ['academy.*.view']` variants.
- **Course/Learning/Instructor routes**: nested under academy or flat student/instructor trees per §5.
- **Platform Owner routes** (`/dashboard/platform/...`): 18 entries as of Prompt 13 — `platform` (dashboard), `platformTrialPolicy`, `platformDomain`, `platformPayments`(+detail), `platformProvisioning`(+detail), `platformOrganizations`(+detail) **[Prompt 13]**, `platformAcademies`(+detail) **[Prompt 13]**, `platformUsers`(+detail) **[Prompt 13]**, `platformRolesPermissions` **[Prompt 13]**, `platformAuditLog`(+detail) **[Prompt 13]**, `platformSupport`(+detail) **[Prompt 13]**, `platformPlanCatalog` **[Prompt 13]**. All gated `requiredRoles: ['platform_owner']`.
- **Public website routes**: not part of `DASHBOARD_ROUTES` at all — resolved entirely inside `PublicWebsiteRouter`, hostname-driven, no auth.
- **System routes**: `/403`, error boundaries.

## Removed in Prompt 13
- `DASHBOARD_ROUTES.billing` (`/dashboard/billing`) — the legacy `BillingPage.tsx` route, deleted along with the page.
- The "Billing" nav entry in `navigation.config.ts`'s Administration section.

## Added in Prompt 13 (navigation)
7 new items in `navigation.config.ts`'s Administration section: Organizations, Academies, Users, Roles & Permissions, Audit Log, Support, Plans & Add-ons — each `requiresAuth: true, requiredRoles: ['platform_owner']`.

## Route guards
Every dashboard route is wrapped `<RouteGuard requireAuthentication ...>` — fail-closed by construction (a route that forgets this defaults to denying access, not granting it). This has been a grep-verified standing practice since a Prompt 3B regression. Prompt 13's 13 new routes were verified via `npx tsc`+manual read, all correctly set.

# 12. Permissions / Security

## Authorization model
- **`RouteGuard`** (`src/app/routes/guards/`) — the sole route-level enforcement point. Fail-closed: a route with no explicit `requireAuthentication`/`requiredPermissions`/`requiredRoles` denies rather than allows.
- **Permission helpers** — `usePermissions()` (`src/shared/hooks/usePermissions.ts`) → `hasPermission`/`hasAllPermissions`/`hasAnyPermission`/`canView`/`canEdit`/`canDelete`/`canManage`, all delegating to `AuthorizationService` (`src/services/identity/authorization.service.ts`), which operates on flat `readonly string[]` arrays.
- **`platform_owner` scope**: a role string (`user.roles.includes('platform_owner')`), checked via `requiredRoles` at the route level — structurally distinct from any permission string. Every Platform Owner Control Plane route added in Prompt 13 uses this gate.
- **Tenant scope**: `requiredPermissions: ['tenant.*.view']`-style checks, backed by `organizationId`-scoped query keys.
- **Academy scope**: `requiredPermissions: ['academy.*.view']`-style checks, backed by `academyId`-scoped query keys.
- **Fail-closed behavior**: confirmed structural, not conventional — grep-verified per prompt since Prompt 3B.
- **Cross-tenant isolation**: every Tenant/Academy/Student-scoped query key embeds its scope id directly (§5). Platform Owner Control Plane keys are deliberately unscoped (cross-tenant by design) but are ONLY reachable behind the `platform_owner` role gate — there is no code path where a non-Platform-Owner session can construct or read a Platform-scoped query key through the UI.
- **Sensitive data restrictions**: `PlatformUserSummary`/`PlatformUserDetail` (Prompt 13) deliberately exclude credentials, tokens, and session data — verified by reading the type file's own doc comment and its field list.

## What MUST NOT be changed casually
- Never bypass `RouteGuard`.
- Never bypass `usePermissions()`/`AuthorizationService` — no direct `user.roles.includes(...)` check inline in a component where the hook exists.
- Never expose cross-tenant data — every new query key must embed its correct scope id, or be Platform-scoped AND role-gated.
- Never hardcode organization/academy/user IDs anywhere in source.
- Never expose secrets — confirmed zero hardcoded credential-shaped strings repo-wide (grep-verified in Prompt 13's validation pass, §22).
- Never weaken authorization to make a new feature "easier."
- `isSafeExternalUrl` (`src/features/website/utils/url-safety.utils.ts`) remains the one and only URL-scheme validator (rejects `javascript:`/`data:`/`vbscript:`/`file:`) — reused, never reimplemented per field.
- No client-side infrastructure/provider credentials — `InfrastructureProviderStatus.connected` remains the only signal exposed, a boolean.
- No card data (`cardNumber`/`cvv`/`expiry`) is ever collected or stored in the frontend.
- JSON-LD structured data is injected via `document.createElement('script').textContent = JSON.stringify(...)` — never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. This remains true after Prompt 13's `buildCourseJsonLd` wiring.

# 13. Localization

`react-i18next`, EN + AR, LTR + RTL. Resource files: `src/localization/resources/{en,ar}/<namespace>.json`, registered in `src/localization/resources/index.ts` and `TRANSLATION_NAMESPACES` (`src/types/localization.types.ts`).

**34 namespaces as of Prompt 13** (was ~26 before): `common`, `navigation`, `validation`, `errors`, `layout`, `home`, `dashboard`, `auth`, `profile`, `settings`, `notifications`, `billing` (legacy namespace — file still exists, no longer consumed by a deleted page; flagged for a future small-issues sweep to confirm remaining usage), `analytics`, `platform`, `search`, `academy`, `course`, `learning`, `instructor`, `announcements`, `blog`, `forum`, `tenant`, `payments`, `provisioning`, `website`, **`auditLog`** (new, Prompt 13), **`support`** (new, Prompt 13), **`media`** (new, Prompt 13).

## Rule for adding new keys
Add to both `en/<ns>.json` and `ar/<ns>.json` in the same edit. Verify parity programmatically — a small Node script comparing flattened key sets, run for every namespace touched, before considering the change complete. Every prompt from 9 onward has done this; Prompt 13 additionally ran a **repository-wide** parity check across all 34 namespaces as part of its final validation, confirming 0 mismatches.

Real tenant-authored content (course titles, website page content, CMS entries) is **not** a translation key — only Atlas's own UI chrome is.

## Known conventions
- Key naming: `<namespace>:<section>.<subsection>.<key>`, camelCase leaves.
- A namespace's JSON structure should mirror the components that consume it — Prompt 13 found and fixed multiple cases (Analytics, Notifications, Settings, Profile) where the JSON had drifted out of sync with actual `t('...')` call sites, sometimes never having matched at all since the file was first scaffolded.

## How to add a new translation (for a future developer)
1. Identify the correct namespace (or create one: add the JSON files, register in `resources/index.ts` and `TRANSLATION_NAMESPACES`).
2. Add the key to `en/<ns>.json` AND `ar/<ns>.json` in the same commit.
3. Run a parity check (flatten both files' keys, diff the sets) before considering the change done.
4. Never leave a component referencing a key that doesn't exist in the JSON — grep for the key string after adding the component code, not before, to catch drift.

# 14. Design System / Component Architecture

- **shadcn/ui primitives**: `src/components/ui/` — Button, Input, Select, Switch, Dialog, Tabs, Card, Badge, Alert, Skeleton, Textarea, Label, Checkbox, ScrollArea, Chart (recharts wrapper, first real consumer wired in Prompt 13's `AnalyticsLineChart`), etc. Reuse these; never hand-roll an equivalent.
- **Shared composed components**: `src/shared/components/`:
  - `layout/` — `PageContainer`, `PageHeader` (title/description/actions slot).
  - `feedback/` — `ErrorState` (the one error presentation, with `onRetry`/`requestId`), `EmptyState` (the one empty presentation, with optional `primaryAction`).
  - `data-display/` — `StatusBadge` (labelKey + `StatusTone`), `MetricCard` (label/value/icon/trend, used by Platform Dashboard and Analytics).
  - `table/` — `DataTable` (the one table component; every Prompt 13 list page — Organizations/Academies/Users/Audit Log/Support — uses it with `usePagination`/`useSearch`).
  - `controls/`, `navigation/`, `branding/`, `loading/`.
- **Forms**: React Hook Form + Zod, `@hookform/resolvers/zod`. `src/components/ui/form.tsx` provides `Form`/`FormField`/`FormItem`/`FormLabel`/`FormControl`/`FormMessage` (a shadcn wrapper — note its `FormMessage` renders `error.message` literally, not through `t()`; some Prompt 13 forms instead render `t(errors.field.message)` manually, matching the wider codebase's convention of Zod messages being literal translation keys — be aware of this inconsistency if touching form error rendering).
- **Status badges**: always via `StatusBadge` + a domain-specific `get<X>StatusTone(status): StatusTone` utility function (never an inline color/variant decision). Prompt 13 added: `platform-status.utils.ts` (Organization/Academy/User + duplicated Provisioning/WebsitePublish tone mappers), `support-status.utils.ts`.
- **Modal/dialog patterns**: shadcn `Dialog` (`Dialog`/`DialogContent`/`DialogHeader`/`DialogTitle`/`DialogDescription`), controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange`. `MediaLibraryDialog` (Prompt 13) is the newest example.
- **What should be reused instead of duplicated**: `DataTable`+`usePagination`+`useSearch` for any list; `ErrorState`/`EmptyState` for any query result; `MetricCard` for any KPI card; `StatusBadge` for any status; `useFilePicker`+base64 for any single-field upload (or `MediaLibraryDialog` where a shared, reusable, listable asset makes more sense — Prompt 13's new option, not a replacement).

# 18. Backend Implementation Roadmap

This section explains what a backend team needs to build, organized by domain, based strictly on the frontend contracts documented in §9. **Nothing here is implemented.** Distinguish three categories throughout: **DEFINED REQUIREMENT** (the frontend has a complete, stable contract — build to it), **FRONTEND CONTRACT** (same meaning, used interchangeably), **BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED** (the frontend deliberately left this open — a human must decide before any code is written).

### Platform Owner Control Plane (Organizations/Academies/Users/Audit Log/Support/Plan Catalog)
- DEFINED REQUIREMENT: `GET /organizations`, `GET /organizations/:id`, `GET /platform-academies`, `GET /platform-academies/:id`, `GET /platform-users`, `GET /platform-users/:id`, `GET /audit-log`, `GET /audit-log/:id`, `GET /support-cases`, `GET /support-cases/:id`, `PATCH /support-cases/:id/status`, `POST /support-cases/:id/messages`. All paginated (page/pageSize), searchable, sortable per `CollectionQuery`.
- Authorization: every one of these must be enforced backend-side as Platform-Owner-only (`platform_owner` role), independent of the frontend's route gate.
- BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED: whether `platform-academies`/`platform-users` are real separate REST resources or views/joins over the same `academies`/`users` tables the tenant-scoped endpoints use — the frontend does not require a particular backend data model, only these response shapes.
- Audit Log specifically: the backend must WRITE an entry on every action it considers auditable. The frontend has no write path for audit entries and none should be added.
- Support Operations: no case-creation endpoint is defined (none is in the frontend contract) — if support cases should be creatable from the dashboard, that is a new requirement needing its own specification, not something to infer from this document.

### Roles & Permissions
- BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED, entirely: no `Role`/`Permission` entity, no catalog endpoint, no assignment endpoint exists in any frontend contract. If real RBAC administration is wanted, it needs its own specification (entity shape, catalog endpoint, assignment endpoint, scope model) before any frontend or backend work begins.
- What IS defined: `CurrentUser.roles`/`CurrentUser.permissions` as flat string arrays, already served by the existing `GET /users/me` (`CurrentUserService.getCurrent`).

### Platform Dashboard / Analytics
- DEFINED REQUIREMENT: `GET /platform-metrics` (singleton, 7 fields). `GET /analytics/overview?from&to`, `GET /analytics/time-series/:metric?from&to`, `GET /analytics/breakdown/:dimension?from&to`.
- BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED: which `metric`/`dimension` string values are valid (the frontend currently calls `time-series` with `'users'`/`'engagement'`/`'revenue'` and `breakdown` with `'plan'` — these are the only ones the UI currently requests, but the contract itself accepts any string).

### Notifications
- DEFINED REQUIREMENT: `GET /notifications`, `GET /notifications/summary`, `PATCH /notifications/:id/read`, `POST /notifications/read-all`, `GET /notifications/preferences`, `PATCH /notifications/preferences`.
- BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED: how notifications are created (what backend-side events generate them) — out of frontend scope entirely.

### Search
- DEFINED REQUIREMENT: `GET /search?q=...` returning `SearchResults` grouped by `SearchResultCategory` (`'users'|'platform'|'content'|'system'`).
- Authorization: the backend MUST apply its own role/permission-aware result scoping — the frontend's client-side category filter is a defensive UX layer only, never the security boundary.
- BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED: what gets indexed and how (search backend technology, ranking) — entirely a backend decision.

### Settings
- DEFINED REQUIREMENT: `GET /platform-settings`, `PATCH /platform-settings` (accepts a partial `PlatformConfiguration`).
- Fields: `platformName` (required string), `platformDescription?`, `supportEmail?`, `twoFactorRequired` (boolean), `sessionTimeoutMinutes` (`15|30|60|'never'`).

### Media Library
- DEFINED REQUIREMENT: `GET /academies/:id/media`, `POST /academies/:id/media` (body: `{fileName, mimeType, sizeBytes, dataUrl, altText?}`), `PATCH /academies/:id/media/:assetId` (body: `{altText?}`), `POST /academies/:id/media/:assetId/archive`.
- BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED: whether the backend accepts base64 `dataUrl` directly (matching the frontend's current, only-existing upload convention) or requires the frontend to move to multipart/presigned-URL — the latter would need frontend changes and should be raised as a decision, not assumed.
- Persistence requirement (inferable): the backend must actually store the asset bytes somewhere (object storage) and return a durable `url` — no frontend contract specifies WHERE, only that `MediaAssetSummary.url` must resolve to the stored asset.

### Authentication (registration / password reset)
- DEFINED REQUIREMENT: `POST /auth/register` (body: `{name, email, password}`, no response body expected — the frontend navigates to sign-in on success, does not expect an auto-login). `POST /auth/password-reset/request` (body: `{email}`). `POST /auth/password-reset/confirm` (body: `{token, newPassword}`).
- BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED: the actual email-delivery mechanism for the reset link/token — entirely backend/infra.

### Profile
- DEFINED REQUIREMENT (already existed pre-Prompt-13, now genuinely exercised): `PATCH /users/me` (body: `{name?, avatar?}` only — no `phone`/`bio`/`email` fields, these were deliberately removed from the frontend form because no contract supports them). `PATCH /users/me/preferences` (body: `{notifications?: {email, push, sms}, theme?, language?}`). `POST /users/me/password` (body: `{currentPassword, newPassword}`).
- BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED: if `phone`/`bio`/email-change/2FA/session-management are wanted, each needs its own new contract — none exists today.

### Billing / Payments
- Unchanged from Prompt 6/7 (`Reports/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s Prompt 6/7 sections have the exhaustive contract). Prompt 13 only removed the legacy fake surface; it did not change any real billing contract.

### Website/CMS/Public Runtime/Provisioning/Domains
- Unchanged from Prompt 8/9/10/11 (`Reports/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s respective sections have the exhaustive contracts). Prompt 13's only change here was wiring `resolveCourseSeo`/`buildCourseJsonLd` into the live public page — a pure frontend rendering change, no new backend requirement beyond what Prompt 9/10/11 already specified (the existing `CourseService`/`PublicWebsiteService` contracts).

# 19. Explicitly Deferred / Undefined

### Plan/Add-on CRUD
Why deferred: no create/update/delete mutation for `Plan`/`AddOn` is specification-supported anywhere (`PlanService` confirmed 100% read-only for the catalog, verified by direct code inspection in Prompt 12 and re-confirmed in Prompt 13). What is needed: a real product decision on whether Plan/Add-on administration should exist in-app at all, and if so, the mutation contract shape. Who needs to decide: the product owner. Do NOT implement until: a real specification (not this document's inference) defines the mutation contract.

### Roles & Permissions catalog/assignment
Why deferred: no `Role`/`Permission` entity type, no catalog endpoint, no assignment endpoint exists anywhere in the codebase or any Reports document. What is needed: entity shape, catalog endpoint, assignment endpoint, scope model (global vs. per-organization vs. per-academy). Who needs to decide: the product owner, likely with input from whoever designs the real backend authorization model. Do NOT implement until: a real RBAC specification exists — do not infer role/permission names from usage patterns in this codebase (they are all currently free-form, backend-defined strings with no frontend-side vocabulary to extend from).

### Blog post public detail page
Why deferred: the Website core-page-type vocabulary (`home`/`about`/`courses`/`courseDetails`/`faqs`/`contact`) has no `blogPostDetails` equivalent, and `resolvePathToPage` (`@features/public-website`) has no blog-post URL pattern. Building one is "rebuilding/extending the Website/CMS feature," explicitly out of Prompt 13's scope. What is needed: a product decision that public blog posts should exist, plus a URL pattern, a page/template, and a `coreType` addition. Who needs to decide: the product owner. Do NOT implement until: explicitly requested — `resolveBlogPostSeo` is ready and waiting the moment a page exists to call it.

### 2FA / session management
Why deferred: no 2FA-enrollment contract, no session-listing/revocation contract exists anywhere. The relevant UI controls (`ProfileSecuritySection.tsx`'s "Enable" 2FA button, "Sign out of all devices" button) are `disabled` with a `title` explaining unavailability — not removed, not faked. What is needed: a real 2FA enrollment flow specification (TOTP? SMS? backend-issued QR?) and a real session domain (list active sessions, revoke one/all). Who needs to decide: the product/security owner. Do NOT implement until: specified.

### Infrastructure mutations (DNS/SSL/CDN/Cloudflare)
Why deferred: explicit, repeated, non-negotiable rule since Prompt 8/11 — "no real DNS/SSL/CDN provisioning, no real Cloudflare account, no fake infrastructure of any kind." What is needed: a real infrastructure provider account/contract, decided entirely outside this codebase. Who needs to decide: whoever owns Atlas's actual production infrastructure. Do NOT implement until: real credentials and a real provider integration plan exist — and even then, credentials must never be read by, stored in, or exposed to the frontend (only a boolean `connected` status may ever reach it).

### Real payment provider integration
Why deferred: `PaymentProviderRegistry` currently registers exactly one adapter (`ManualTransferProvider`) — the gateway-adapter seam exists (`GatewayPaymentProviderAdapter`) but has no real gateway plugged in, by design, since Prompt 7. What is needed: a real payment gateway account + SDK + webhook handling, entirely backend/infra work; the frontend adapter seam does not need to change to accommodate it. Who needs to decide: whoever owns Atlas's commercial/financial infrastructure. Do NOT implement until: a real gateway contract is chosen.

### Real storage infrastructure (Media Library / all uploads)
Why deferred: no upload endpoint (multipart or presigned-URL) has ever existed in this codebase, at any prompt. Every "upload" in Atlas — Course thumbnails, Academy branding, Website images, CMS entry images, and now Media Library assets — is a base64 data URL submitted through an ordinary JSON PATCH/POST. What is needed: a real object-storage backend (S3-compatible or equivalent) and a decision on whether to keep the base64 contract or move to multipart/presigned URLs (the latter requires frontend changes too, and should be raised as a decision before backend work begins). Who needs to decide: the backend/infra owner. Do NOT implement a fake storage layer in the frontend under any circumstances — this rule held throughout Prompt 13 and must continue to hold.

# 20. Do Not Break These

- **Do not create a second service architecture.** Every domain follows `Component → Hook → Service (extends BaseService) → apiClient`. Three distinct service-tree-splitting precedents already exist for differing authorization shapes (Instructor/flat-teaching-scope, PlatformPaymentReview/flat-cross-tenant, PublicWebsite/session-less-hostname-resolved) — a fourth genuinely-different-shape domain may follow one of these patterns; do not invent a new pattern for something that fits an existing one. Prompt 13 followed this literally for every new Platform Owner service (flat, cross-tenant, role-gated).
- **Do not bypass hooks.** No direct `fetch`/`axios`/service call from a page or component.
- **Do not bypass query keys.** Every read/write goes through the domain's key factory in `src/services/query/query-keys.ts` — this is how cache scoping and invalidation stay correct.
- **Do not bypass permission helpers.** No inline `user.roles.includes(...)` where `usePermissions()`/`RouteGuard` already exists.
- **Do not invent API responses.** No hardcoded array/object presented as if it came from a network call.
- **Do not use mock data as a backend replacement.** A missing backend is represented by a real query that will fail/be pending until a backend exists — never by fake data that "looks done."
- **Do not use `setTimeout` as fake network behavior.** This was the single most common anti-pattern found and fixed across Prompt 13 (10 total instances across Search, Auth×3, Profile×3, Settings, Feature Flags, Notifications-adjacent) — do not reintroduce it anywhere, ever, for any reason including "just for a quick demo."
- **Do not hardcode metrics.** Every KPI/metric card must trace to a real service method, even if that method has no live backend yet.
- **Do not hardcode entity IDs.** No literal organization/academy/user/course id anywhere in source.
- **Do not weaken authorization** to make a feature easier to build or test.
- **Do not introduce cross-tenant data leakage.** Every new query key must embed its correct scope, or be Platform-scoped and role-gated with no other access path.
- **Do not duplicate billing surfaces.** There are exactly two real billing surfaces (Tenant Billing, Platform Payment Review) — do not add a third.
- **Do not create duplicate routes.** Verified zero duplicates as of Prompt 13's validation; a route path string should exist in exactly one `<Route>`.
- **Do not create new architecture for Platform Owner features.** Every Prompt 13 Platform Owner page/service/hook follows the exact same pattern as every prior domain — this must continue.
- **Do not rebuild Complete domains without a documented reason.** The 9 originally-Complete domains, plus everything Prompt 13 completed, must be extended, not redesigned, unless a real gap is found and documented (as Prompt 13 itself did for Media Library integration into `WebsiteImageField`, and for the Course SEO wiring into `PublicWebsitePage`).
- **Do not invent Role/Permission names, endpoint paths, or business rules** not evidenced by an actual specification, a Reports document, or this handover's explicitly-marked findings.
- **Do not fake infrastructure status.** Domain/SSL/CDN status must always come from a real backend response, never hardcoded "active"/"connected"/"verified" by the frontend.
- **Do not use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`** for anything user/tenant-controlled — the one existing use (`chart.tsx`, shadcn's own vetted component, static CSS variable injection) is pre-existing, untouched, and safe; do not add a second use anywhere else.

# 21. Known Technical Notes

- **Package manager**: npm (evidenced by `package.json`/`package-lock.json` conventions; no `pnpm-lock.yaml`/`yarn.lock` present).
- **Build**: `npm run build` (`vite build`). Succeeds as of the end of Prompt 13; every lazy-loaded page ships its own chunk.
- **Dev**: `npm run dev` (`vite`).
- **Typecheck**: `npm run typecheck` (`tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`).
- **Lint**: `npm run lint` (`eslint --quiet ./src`).
- **Format**: `npm run format` / `npm run format:check` (Prettier).
- **Test**: no `test` script exists in `package.json` — **no automated test suite exists in this repository at any prompt**, including Prompt 13. Validation throughout the project's history has relied on `typecheck`+`lint`+`build`+manual/forensic code-reading audits, never automated tests. Do not assume a test runner exists.
- **Environment variables**: `src/config/env.config.ts` (includes `platformBaseDomain`, `isDevelopment`) — no secret values are ever written into this handover or, per the project's own rules, into the frontend at all.
- **API client**: `src/services/api/api-client.ts` (public entry point) + `http-client.ts` (axios wrapper, attaches auth token "if available," never required — this is how the public website runtime works unauthenticated through the same client).
- **Path aliases**: `@app`, `@components`, `@features`, `@hooks`, `@services`, `@types`, `@utils`, `@api`, `@constants`, `@localization` (see `tsconfig.app.json`'s `paths` for the complete, authoritative list — do not assume an alias exists without checking).
- **Folder conventions**: one directory per feature under `src/features/<name>/`, each optionally with `pages/`, `components/`, `hooks/`, `services/`, `schemas/`, `utils/`, `constants/`, and (only where cross-feature consumption is needed) a curated `index.ts` public barrel.
- **Naming conventions**: `Website*` prefix for anything in the website/theme domain (never bare `Theme*` — collides with the dashboard's own theme system); `Platform*` prefix for Platform Owner Control Plane services/pages (Prompt 13); services named `<Domain>Service`, hooks named `use<Verb><Domain>`; query-key factories named `<domain>Keys`.
- **`no-restricted-imports` ESLint rule**: only bare `@features/<name>` barrel imports are allowed cross-feature (never `@features/<name>/<deep-path>`) — this is why Prompt 13's cross-feature reuse (Media Library into Website, Audit Log into Platform, Plan Catalog into Platform, Course into Public Website) each required or used an existing public barrel, and why some tone-mapping utilities were deliberately duplicated (a few lines) rather than deep-imported across features without one.
- **Important configuration files**: `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.app.json` (path aliases), `eslint.config.js` (the `no-restricted-imports` rule lives here), `tailwind.config.ts`.

# 23. How Future Claude Should Work

1. **Read this file (`ATLAS_HANDOVER.md`) completely** before making any change.
2. **Read `Reports/ARCHITECTURE.md`** — at minimum the per-prompt section relevant to whatever domain you're about to touch; it has exhaustive file lists and backend-contract detail this document deliberately does not fully reproduce for Prompts 1–12 (to avoid drift between two sources of the same truth).
3. **Read `Reports/PROGRESS.md`** (Requirements Overview + Task Breakdown) for the relevant prompt(s).
4. **Inspect the relevant domain directly in `src/`** before assuming this document's characterization is still accurate — it is a snapshot as of the end of Prompt 13, not a live view.
5. **Never assume a missing backend implementation means the frontend is missing.** As of Prompt 13, every domain in §17 marked "FRONTEND READY, BACKEND PENDING" has a complete, real frontend — the absence of a backend is expected and correct, not a gap to "fix" by faking one.
6. **Reuse the existing Service → QueryKeys → Hooks → Types/Zod → Pages → Routes/Nav architecture** for anything new. Do not invent a fifth service-tree pattern when one of the four existing ones (nested-tenant-scoped, flat-role-resolved-teaching-scope, flat-cross-tenant-platform-scope, session-less-hostname-scoped) already fits.
7. **Check this handover, then `Reports/ATOMS.md`'s Key Decisions table**, before modifying architecture — most "don't do this" rules are captured in one or the other.
8. **Check existing types and contracts first** (§9/§10) before writing a new type — several Prompt 13 domains deliberately reused existing types verbatim (`TenantSubscription`, `AcademyStatus`, `ProvisioningStatus`, `WebsitePublishStatus`, `DomainStatus`, `Plan`, `AddOn`, `NotificationPreferences`) rather than re-deriving them.
9. **Do not invent requirements.** If a business rule, permission name, endpoint shape, or KPI is not evidenced by an actual specification, a Reports document, or this handover's explicitly-marked findings, it does not exist yet.
10. **Ask for clarification when the specification is genuinely undefined** — §19 lists every currently-known undefined boundary. Extend that list (do not silently invent) if a new one is discovered.

## How to safely begin backend implementation
Start with the domains in §17 marked "FRONTEND READY, BACKEND PENDING" that have the simplest, most self-contained contracts and the fewest BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED items (§18): Platform Dashboard/Metrics, Audit Log (read side), Notifications, Settings, and the read-only Platform Owner consoles (Organizations/Academies/Users) are all good starting points — each is a small number of endpoints with a fully-specified request/response shape and no open product questions. Defer Media Library (has one open BACKEND DECISION REQUIRED — base64 vs. multipart) and anything in §19 (genuinely undefined) until those decisions are made. Billing/Payments/Provisioning/Website/Public-Runtime already have exhaustive contracts documented in `Reports/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s Prompt 6–11 sections and may proceed in parallel at any time — they were never blocked by Prompt 13.
